Replay

Replay Quickdraw

4 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Authored rule correspondenceWhat the gates establish

A separate port of Kit Quickdraw. The original project remains runnable. Gameplay lives in shared/duel, a pure Odin complete-world model; Godot supplies input, scene instances and presentation.

From the repository root:

Shell
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_quickdraw/play.sh
nix develop --command bash tests/replay_quickdraw/run.sh
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_quickdraw/run.sh
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_quickdraw/network_run.sh
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_quickdraw/migration_run.sh
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_quickdraw/early_claim_run.sh
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_quickdraw/early_claim_fault_run.sh

The interactive default opens the session menu. Choose Solo, Host, Join or Watch; Host waits for the match leader to press Start. Name, address and port are editable. Explicit roles retain the scripted automatic-start path, for example:

Shell
RQ_ROLE=host nix develop --command bash examples/replay_quickdraw/play.sh
RQ_ROLE=client nix develop --command bash examples/replay_quickdraw/play.sh

RQ_ROLE also accepts server (no local avatar) and observer. RQ_PORT defaults to 49460. Direct native launchers use the configured address. The party interface now provides service-backed creation/invites/rejoin, native ENet and browser WebRTC; public deployment remains unverified. The Room driver is enabled by RQ_COORD_PORT with explicitly provisioned RQ_MEMBER, RQ_INCARNATION, RQ_COORD_KEY and RQ_TOKEN. These credentials retain the existing automatic Room launch when RQ_ROLE is omitted; RQ_AUTO=0 leaves launch to the menu. The migration harness launches an isolated coordinator and provisions three local members; the first two are trusted hosts. RQ_LATENCY injects receive delay in milliseconds; RQ_JITTER, RQ_LOSS and RQ_DUPLICATE configure the existing transport fault adapter (loss/duplication in ten-thousandths).

Enter focuses chat, Escape releases it, and Tab shows the scoreboard. Typing captures movement, drone steering and combat/shop input while simulation continues. WASD moves, mouse aims, left click fires, Space dashes, right click lobs, B buys boots, and IJKL steers your independent drone. RQ_GOLD=1 starts each player with one coin for the shop scenario. Test bots are strafer, deadeye, orbit and lobber; set RQ_BOT to select one. RQ_NOREWIND=1 on the authority is the live collision A/B control. RQ_NOLOB=1 isolates hitscan.

Authored rule correspondence#

The port preserves the 640×360 arena, 12-pixel walls, two crates, four spawn points, 9-pixel body radius, movement/dash speeds and cadence, three HP, 120-tick respawn, hitscan cover/range, one-gold boots and their 1.3× speed multiplier, independent drone steering/clamp, and lob speed/lifetime/radius/cooldown. Hitscan kills award one gold; lob kills award score without gold, as in the original. Gold uses the original eight-bit storage. Death freezes body/weapon cooldowns and respawn retains equipment and those cooldowns. Dedicated seats are numbered differently: a spawn offset gives the first two clients the original dedicated duel's bottom lane.

The world now owns HP, gold, score, respawn schedules, entity lifetime and collision history in the same replayable state. The original mixes simulation and discrete replication fields. Historical target life IDs deliberately reject hits against a previous incarnation after respawn. The port defines a stable system order: movement, proxy recording, existing lobs, then new fire/lobs in seat order.

Scene geometry and view assets come from the original; see provenance. The HUD and session interface are a separate implementation. The session UI now has named chat, a scoreboard, manual start, leave/rejoin and local identity/name preferences. Combat feedback now restores sampled hurt flashes and independent material colors, and adds event-driven landing rings. Native saves now support F5/Save, exact solo/host resume and fresh-process rejoin. Browser parties now pass combat, planned/crash migration, observer rejoin and durable Room publication. Browser-local slots now support durable solo save/resume, stale-tab refusal and corruption preservation. Public/Steam deployment, human visual/play-feel review and a paired old/new benchmark remain pending. This is not full Quickdraw or M6 completion.

What the gates establish#

  • Native simulation: interpolated historical hit versus live miss, cover/history misses, respawn identity, dash/drone/cooldown/shop rules, stable predicted spawn IDs, and archive continuation during projectile flight/respawn/queued purchase. WASM is type-checked; cross-target deterministic execution is not claimed.
  • Solo Godot: scene initialization, movement/combat loop and purchase.
  • Three-process ENet: two 30-second hitscan phases at 120 ms injected delay per network leg, followed by a lob/purchase phase. The gate requires a clear historical/live hit gap, matching authoritative totals, one shot effect per authoritative shot on the shooter/observer, every lob predicted before authority acknowledgement, and the corresponding Godot node visible in less than 120 ms.
  • Four-process migration: coordinator, host, successor and surviving shooter at 240 ms gameplay RTT. Planned handoff and a killed host both restore an exact approved combat frame, including projectile flight and respawn/cooldown/history state, then continue shooting/purchasing. Clients compare canonical world digests at a common tick. The planned source rejoins with its original seat.

RQ_METRICS prints simulation correction/replay counts, application bytes and lob input-to-node latency. That latency measures input sampling to scene-node presence; it does not measure display scanout. Corrections are snapshot applications, not necessarily visible positional errors. Detailed correction magnitude, CPU percentiles, partial prediction, and broader competitive migration/fault scenarios remain acceptance work.

See aim/view context for the authoring contract and the limits of timestamp validation. Retain both projects when comparing them.

The early-claim gate exercises a rejected takeover while the owner is still live, verifies that preparation resumes with a fresh backup, then crashes the owner during a longer combat run. REPLAY_MIGRATION_TRACE=1 logs coordinator/backup frontiers; REPLAY_KEEP_LOGS=1 retains process output. For focused diagnosis, REPLAY_MIGRATION_PHASE=crash selects only the crash phase of migration_run.sh; its sentinel distinguishes that subset from the complete migration gate.
